rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies the people who received Scripture here as Jewish scholars; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima.
rows.anchor: ذهب إبن جبيروهو المروى عن إبن عباس من طريق عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Alqama expands the referent to include Jewish and Christian scholars.
rows.anchor: وإما ما يشملهم وأحبار النصارى وهو المروي عنه من طريق علقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them recipients of Scripture either heightens the censure of their conduct or hints that their covenant was written in the Scripture they received.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكروا بعنوان إيتاء الكتاب مبالغة في تقبيح حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the covenant had been recorded in their revealed book.
rows.anchor: وقيل : رمزا إلى أن أخذ الميثاق كان في كتابهم الذي أوتوه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that Abd Allah’s companions recited the verse with “your Lord” taking their covenant.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير أن أصحاب عبدالله يقرؤنوإذ أخذ ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to the covenant carries an oath sense; its pronoun refers to the Book, which they must disclose with all its rulings and reports, especially Muhammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: جواب ميثاق لتضمنه معنى القسم والضمير للكتاب أي بالله لتظهرن جميع ما فيه

rows.speaker: السدي وابن جبير
rows.claim: The apparent wording attributed to al-Suddi and Ibn Jubayr instead takes the pronoun to refer to Muhammad, though he is not named explicitly.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلام السدي وإبن جبير أن الضمير لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية ابن عياش
rows.claim: These readers have the third-person reading ليبيننه, with yāʾ of absence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية ابن عياش ليبيننه بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits reporting an oath in third-person, second-person, or first-person form; the verse at 27:49 illustrates the forms لنبيتنه and its reported variants.
rows.anchor: إذا أخبرت عن يمين حلف بها فلك في ذلك ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تكتمونه coordinates with the oath’s response and lacks emphatic nūn because it is negative; Abu al-Baqa says the first verb’s emphasis suffices.
rows.anchor: عطف على الجواب وإنما لم يؤكد بالنون لكونه منفيا وقال أبو البقاء : إكتفاء بالتوكيد في الفعل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative clause may be circumstantial, either with an omitted subject after wāw or by allowing wāw before a negative imperfect in a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون حالا من ضمير المخاطبين إما على إضمار مبتدأ بعد الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prohibiting concealment after commanding disclosure intensifies the obligation; alternatively, disclosure means stating proofs of Muhammad’s prophethood while concealment means suppressing strained interpretations and false doubts.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن الكتمان بعد الأمر بالبيان للمبالغة في إيجاب المأمور به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glossed disclosure and nonconcealment as speaking the truth and confirming it through action; the author says the prohibition following the command may make this reading more useful.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أنه كان يفسر ( لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه ) بقوله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ومن معه
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and other readers recite ولا يكتمونه with yāʾ of absence, matching the preceding verb’s reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ومن معه ولا يكتمونه بالياء كما في سابقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cast the covenant behind their backs by disregarding it entirely; the image is a metaphor for neglect and inattention, opposite placing something before one’s eyes.
rows.anchor: أي طرحوا ما أخذ منهم من الميثاق وراء ظهورهم ولم يراعوه ولم يلتفتوا إليه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “they bought with it,” the pronoun preferably refers to the Book they were ordered to disclose and not conceal; the purchase was taking something in exchange for it.
rows.anchor: بالكتاب الذي أمروا ببيانه ونهوا عن كتمانه وقيل : الضمير للعهد والأول أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the pronoun in “with it” refer to the covenant.
rows.anchor: كتمانه وقيل : الضمير للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small price is the transient debris of worldly life and its corrupt aims.
rows.anchor: من حطام الدنيا الفانية وأغراضها الفاسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one grammatical analysis, ما is an indefinite accusative explaining the subject of biʾsa, يشترونه is its descriptive clause, and the specific object of blame is omitted.
rows.anchor: ما نكرو منصوبة مفسرة لفاعل بئسوجملة يشترونه صفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما is a verbal noun serving as the subject of biʾsa; the omitted object of blame is their purchase, which merits painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( ما ) مصدرية فاعلبئس والمخصوص محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the duty to disclose religious knowledge and the ban on concealing it for corrupt ends such as appeasing oppressors or courting their favor.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على وجوب إظهار العلم وحرمة كتمان شيء من أمور الدين لغرض فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith warns that whoever is asked about knowledge and conceals it will be bridled with fire.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر من سئل عن علم فكتمه ألجم بلجام من نار

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Umara recounts that he quoted Ali’s saying to al-Zuhri: God required the learned to teach before requiring the ignorant to learn; al-Zuhri then narrated forty reports.
rows.anchor: عن نجم الخراز قال : سمعت علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra said he would not have related reports to the audience but for God’s covenant with the People of Scripture, and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن أبي هريرة لولا ما أخذ الله تعالى على أهل الكتاب ما حدثتكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan said he would not have told people much of what they ask without God’s covenant with people of knowledge; the author presents this as support for the duty to disclose.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن لولا الميثاق الذي أخذه الله تعالى على أهل العلم ما حدثتكم بكثير مما تسألون عنه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda relates that a visitor told a mosque gathering including Ibn Masud that Kaʿb said the verse was not about them; Ibn Masud sent Kaʿb greetings and answered that it was revealed while Kaʿb was a Jew.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة قال : جاء رجل إلى قوم في المسجد وفيهم عبدالله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud meant that Kaʿb had not understood the verse’s allusion, even though it was revealed about the People of Scripture.
rows.anchor: وأراد إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أن كعبا لم يعرف ماأشارت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition لا تحسبن addresses the Prophet or any suitable addressee and means not to suppose.
rows.anchor: خطاب لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أو لكل أحد ممن يصلح للخطاب أي لا تظنن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase بما أتوا means what they did; Ubayy has this reading, while بما آتوا and بما أوتوا are also recited, the latter reported from Ali.
rows.anchor: أي بما فعلوا وبه قرأ أبي وقريء ( بما آتوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people whose praise they seek may be people generally, Muslims, or the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أن يحمدهم الناس وقيل : المسلمون وقيل : رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through al-Awfi, Ibn Abbas identifies the people as the People of Scripture, who judged falsely and distorted words, then sought praise for prayers and fasting they had not performed.
rows.anchor: هم أهل الكتاب أنزل عليهم الكتاب فحكموا بغير الخحق وحرفوا الكلام عن مواضعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says they concealed the Prophet’s question, gave a false answer, and left wanting praise as if they had answered him truthfully.
rows.anchor: قال إبن عباس فيما أخرجه عنه إبن أبي حاتم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they rejoiced at concealing their Scripture’s description of the Prophet and wanted to be praised as followers of Abraham’s religion.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد إبن جبير أنهم ( يفرحون ) بكتمانهم صفة رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s interpretation, the relative pronoun refers to the previously mentioned covenant-takers, replacing their pronoun; the clause explains their deeds and their resulting punishment, while also offering consolation.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون الموصول عبارة عن المذكورين سابقا الذين أخذ ميثاقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also exposes their persistence in wrongdoing, delight in it, and wish to be credited with fine qualities they lack; the wording presents this conduct as notorious.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك من التسلية أيضا ما لا يخفى وقد أدمج فيها بيان بعض آخر من شنائعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the referent as a known group of hypocrites, including some of the earlier people and others; a report from Abu Saʿid describes hypocrites staying behind during a campaign, rejoicing, then seeking praise after the Prophet returned.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الموصول عبارة عن أناس منافقين وهم طائفة معهودون

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that hypocrites rejoiced at remaining behind when the Prophet went to war, then apologized and swore when he returned, hoping to be praised for what they had not done; the verse was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: أن رجالا من المنافقين كانوا إذا خرج رسول الله

rows.speaker: رافع بن خديج وزيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: The source says a similar report is also transmitted from Rafiʿ ibn Khadij, Zayd ibn Thabit, and others.
rows.anchor: وروى مثل ذلك عن رافع بن خديج وزيد بن ثابت وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies the people as all hypocrites, most of whom were Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بهؤلاء المنافقون كافة وقد كان أكثرهم من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some argue the hypocrite reading best fits the clause: they rejoiced in outwardly professing faith while inwardly disbelieving and sought Muslim praise for faith they did not practice, despite their hostility to believers.
rows.anchor: وأدعى بعضهم أنه الأنسب بما في حيز الصلة لشهرة أنهم كانوا يفرحون بما فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this fit is not supported, so far as he knows, by sound reports.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه لم يوجد فيما نعلم من الآثار الصحيحة ما يؤيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is far-fetched to make the relative pronoun universal, covering anyone who admires good deeds and wants praise for qualities they lack.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم بعد القول بأن الأولى إجراء الموصول على عمومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To include the earlier covenant-takers directly, that universal interpretation must broaden بما أتوا to cover both real and unreal good deeds; if it means good deeds alone, they did no actual good deed to rejoice over.
rows.anchor: أما إذا خص بالحسنات كما يوهمه ظاهر هذا القول فلا يسلم الانتظام

rows.speaker: مروان
rows.claim: Marwan objected that if everyone who rejoices in what they receive and seeks undeserved praise is punished, then all people will be punished.
rows.anchor: أن مروان قال لبوابه : أذهب يارافع إلى إبن عباس فقل : لئن كان كل أمريء منا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas replied that the verse was revealed about the People of Scripture, then recited the covenant passage through the following verse.
rows.anchor: فقال إبن عباس : ما لكم ولهذه الآية إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ibn Abbas understood the verse universally, he could have resolved Marwan’s concern by restricting the joy to self-admiration; his answer does not show that such joy and undeserved praise are never forbidden.
rows.anchor: لو كان الأولى إجراء الموصول على عمومه لأجراه خبر الأمة وترجمان القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other texts clearly prohibit self-admiring joy and seeking praise for what one has not done, and some scholars count this among major sins.
rows.anchor: وكثير من النصوص ناطق بحرمة ذلك حتى عده البعض من الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either interpretation, the relative clause is the first object of لا تحسبن and فلا تحسبنهم confirms it; Arabic repeats hasiba after a long account to mark continuity and reinforce the statement, as al-Zajjaj explains.
rows.anchor: والعربكما قال الزجاجإذا أطالت القصة تعيد حسبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ before فلا تحسبنهم is extra, as illustrated by the poetic example continued in the next segment.
rows.anchor: والفاء زائدة كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic line فإذا هلكت فعند ذلك فأجزعي illustrates the extra fāʾ discussed in the preceding segment.
rows.anchor: فإذا هلكت ( فعند ) ذلك فأجزعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second object means being in a state of deliverance from punishment; here مفازة is a verbal noun for success, and its tāʾ is part of that noun form rather than a singular marker.
rows.anchor: أي متلبسين بنجاة منه على أن المفازة مصدر ميمي بمعنى الفوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, مفازة is a place of safety, metaphorically a barren plain; then من العذاب modifies it, since a place noun cannot govern, and a specific implied relation meaning safe from punishment is required.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون المفازة اسم مكان أي محل فوز ونجاة وأن يستعار من المفازة للقفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic implied sense “existing from punishment” is invalid because the place is not made from punishment; critics also call the special implied relation strained and unnecessary.
rows.anchor: لأن المفازة ليست من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readings put ḍamma on the bāʾ in both verbs and address believers too; other readings use third-person yāʾ with fatḥa, with the objects as previously explained.
rows.anchor: وقريء بضم الباء الموحدة في الفعلين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
rows.claim: They read the first verb in third person with fatḥa and the second in third person with ḍamma; the rejoicing people are the first verb’s subject, its objects are supplied by the second, and they must not suppose themselves safe.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير بالياء وفتح الباء في الفعل الأول وبالياء وضم الباء في الفعل الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis deletes the first object and states the second: the people must not suppose themselves safe; the second clause confirms the first and its fāʾ is extra.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفعول الأولللايحسبنمحذوفا والمفعول الثاني مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis states both objects, with their pronoun attached to the second verb and مفازة as the second object, treating only the verb and subject as repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ضميرهم المتصل بالفعل الثاني والثاني ( بمفازة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That analysis is objected to because it attaches an object pronoun to something other than its governor or the governor’s subject; the author notes that many grammarians allow this construction and the matter has been treated separately.
rows.anchor: ورد بأن فيه اتصال ضمير المفعول بغير عامله أو فاعله المتصل بعامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis makes the first verb’s subject the Prophet or any reckoner, with the relative clause as its object and the second verb’s omitted object understood from the stated pronoun and مفازة; the fāʾ then coordinates the consequence.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون الفعل الأول مسندا إلى ضمير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو كل حاسب

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: He explains that the warning begins by forbidding their assumption to expose their weak views and empty hopes: they thought their worldly escape meant they would escape the afterlife too; the Prophet’s prohibition insinuates their belief rather than doubting his own judgment.
rows.anchor: لتنبيه على بطلان آرائهم الركيكة وقطع أطماعهم الفارغة حيث كانوا يزعمون أنهم ينجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the relative pronoun is universal, the reason for opening with this prohibition is unclear unless one invokes grammatical predominance.
rows.anchor: على تقدير إجراء الموصول على عمومه على ما مر غير ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their painful punishment establishes a punishment without limit in duration or severity after the preceding denial of escape from punishment generally; the nominal sentence, emphatic indefiniteness, and description signal this.
rows.anchor: بيان لثبوت فرد من العذاب لا غاية له في المدة والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this refers to punishment in the afterlife, while the earlier denial of safety refers to immediate worldly punishment: disgrace and rejection as their false appearance is exposed.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون هذا إشارة إلى العذاب الأخروي ويحمل نفي النجاة من العذاب فيما تقدم على نفي العذاب العاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address يا أيها الناس applies to accountable people from the revelation of the verse until the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: خطاب يعم المكلفين من لدن نزل إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most jurists say slaves are included in a general address to people because a slave is one of the people and servitude does not itself bar inclusion.
rows.anchor: فذهب الأكثرون إلى التناول لأن العبد من الناس مثلا فيدخل في الخطاب العام له قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some jurists exclude slaves: since their benefits belong to their masters by consensus, a command using their time for another’s benefit would conflict with that rule; their exclusion from jihad, Friday prayer, pilgrimage, and donations is also cited.
rows.anchor: وذهب البعض إلى عدم التناول قالوا : لأنه قد ثبت بالإجماع صرف منافع العبد إلى سيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that the master does not own every benefit: near the end of the noon-prayer window, the slave must pray even if obeying the master would make the prayer lapse.
rows.anchor: بل قد يستثنى من ذلك وقت تضايق العبادات حتى لو أمره السيد في آخر وقت الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusion from some commands does not prove slaves were outside the general address: specific evidence can exclude them, just as illness or travel excludes people from general commands about fasting, prayer, and jihad.
rows.anchor: بأن خروجه بدليل أقتضى خروجه وذلك كخروج المريض والمسافر والحائض عن العمومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples are not included in this address, since commands and prohibitions address those able to comply, whereas earlier generations lie under the earth until the trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: أن الأمم الدارجة قبل نزول هذا الخطاب لاحظ لها فيه لاختصاص الأوامر والنواهي بمن يتصور منه الامتثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some include earlier peoples in the address and in the coming command in God’s eternal speech, though its Arabic form is incidental to this community; the author objects that the discussion concerns Quranic rulings after revelation, or all direct address would be metaphorical.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون الخطاب عاما بحيث يندرجون فيه ثم قال : ولا يبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word الناس includes males and females by agreement, but whether a masculine plural command such as اتقوا ربكم includes women is disputed; most say it does not apparently, unlike the Hanbalis.
rows.anchor: وفي شمول نحو قوله تعالى : ( أتقوا ربكن ( خلاف

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that women asked why God mentioned only men, after which a verse mentioning women was revealed; the majority infer that women were not already included in the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: عن أم سلمة أنها قالت : يارسول الله إن النساء قلن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority also argue that Arabic grammarians classify this form as masculine plural and that adding women in the Quranic phrase المسلمين والمسلمات would be redundant if women were already included in its apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وبأنه قد أجمع أرباب العربية على أن نحو هذه الصيغة جمع مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who include women argue that Arabic convention lets the masculine dominate when the sexes are combined; otherwise women would miss many shared legal rulings, and a bequest to men and women followed by “I bequeathed to them” includes both.
rows.anchor: المعروف من أهل اللسان تغليبهم المذكر على المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report from Umm Salama only proves that the wording can be used for everyone when that is intended; the majority call that figurative, so it does not establish universal apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: فبأنه إنما يدل على أن الإطلاق صحيح إذا قصد الجميع والجمهور يقولون به لكنه يكون مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument from shared legal rulings fails: women can participate through separate evidence, as they do not enter rules for jihad or Friday prayer without such evidence.
rows.anchor: في الأحكام بمثل هذه الصيغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest example does not establish immediate inclusion without context, because the preceding bequest itself signals the intended referent.
rows.anchor: فإن الوصية المتقدمة قرينة دالة على الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes that women are not included in the apparent meaning of the masculine form, though here it is preferable to include them through grammatical predominance.
rows.anchor: فالحق عدم دخول الإناث ظاهرا نعم الأولى هنا القول بدخولهن باعتبار التغليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view that the command addresses men alone and includes women only through external evidence would require restricting الناس, which the author says sound taste rejects.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن لا تغليب بل الأمر للرجال فقط كما يقتضيه ظاهر الصيغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to practice taqwa may broadly mean avoiding disbelief, sins, and vices while honoring both human and divine rights.
rows.anchor: والمأمور به إما الإتقاء بحيث يشمل ما كان بإجتناب الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, taqwa means protecting the rights owed among people; this specifically fits the surah’s concerns with orphans, kinship, marital justice, and inheritance, while the broader reading fits only generally.
rows.anchor: وأما الإتقاء في الإخلال بما يجب حفظه من الحقوق فيما بين العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” supports the command and reinforces the duty to obey.
rows.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضمير المخاطبين ما لا يخفى من تأييد الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing God as the one who created the addressees from one soul functions as a reason for the command; it points either to immense power or great favor, prompting piety through fear or gratitude.
rows.anchor: لأن ما ذكر يدل على القدرة العظيمة أو النعمة الجسيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from one origin especially makes piety compelling if the description is understood as a reminder of favor and the gratitude owed for it.
rows.anchor: وإيجاب الخلق من أصل واحد للإتقاء على الإحتمال الثاني ظاهر جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description also reminds the addressees that they know these facts that call for piety, and rebukes anyone who nevertheless neglects it.
rows.anchor: وفي الوصف المذكور تنبيه على أن المخاطبين عالمون بما ذكر مما يستدعي التحلي بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one soul is Adam, whom the mainstream jurists and traditionists regard as the sole first human and father of humankind.
rows.anchor: والمراد من النفس الواحدة آدم عليه السلام والذي عليه الجماعة من الفقهاء والمحدثين

rows.speaker: صاحب جامع الأخبار
rows.claim: A report in Jamiʿ al-Akhbar says God created thirty Adams, with a thousand years between each, followed by fifty thousand years of desolation, fifty thousand years of habitation, and then our father Adam.
rows.anchor: ذكر صاحب جامع الأخبار من الإمامية في الفصل الخامس عشر خبرا طويلا نقل فيه أن الله تعالى خلق قبل أبينا آدم ثلاثين آدم

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A long report in Ibn Babawayh’s al-Tawhid quotes al-Sadiq saying God created a million Adams and that this humanity is the last of them.
rows.anchor: وروى إبن بابويه في كتاب التوحيد عن الصادق

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Maytham’s commentary on the Nahj quotes Muhammad al-Baqir saying a million or more Adams preceded our father Adam.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن محمد بن علي الباقرأنه قال : قد إنقضى قبل آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عربي
rows.claim: The author says Ibn Arabi’s Futuhat appears to imply that another Adam existed forty thousand years before ours.
rows.anchor: وذكر الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره في فتوحاته ما يقتضي بظاهره أن قبل آدم بأربعين ألف سنة آدم غيره

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report in al-Khasaʾis quotes al-Sadiq saying God has twelve thousand worlds, each larger than seven heavens and seven earths, and each unaware of the other worlds.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق أنه قال : إن لله تعالى إثني عشر ألف عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests such reports may belong to esoteric or imaginal material; if they are sound, multiple Adams there need not mean multiple Adams in this world.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذا وأمثاله من أزض السمسمة وجابر ساوجا بلقا إن صح محمول على عالم المثال

rows.speaker: زين العرب
rows.claim: The author says Sunnis reject literal multiple Adams; Zayn al-Arab even declared a believer in multiple Adams an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: بل قد صرح زين العرب بكفر من يعتقد التعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Our Adam was preceded by other creations such as angels, jinn, and many animals, but not other humans like him; humanity began in time, contrary to philosophers who claim its species is eternal.
rows.anchor: آدمنا هدا عليه السلام مسبوق بخلق آخرين كالملائكة والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Sunnis held that six thousand years elapsed before the Prophet and that the world lasts seven thousand years, relying on many reports.
rows.anchor: وذهب الكثير منا إلى أنه منذ كان إلى زمن البعثة ستة آلاف سنة وأن عمر الدنيا سبعة آلاف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author holds that the world began after not existing and will end; when it began and ends is known only to God, and the reports on its timing are too contradictory to rely on.
rows.anchor: والحق عندي أنه كان بعد أن لم يكن ولا يكون بعد أن كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as neither sound creed nor certainty the claim that a universal soul judges individual souls every seven thousand years and that the Hour follows the thousandth resurrection.
rows.anchor: مما لا أزتضيه دينا ولا أختاره يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربكم and خلقكم address those commanded; extending them to earlier nations while the earlier address excluded them needlessly splits the syntax, since God’s lordship and creation of the addressees already encompass their ancestors.
rows.anchor: للمأمورين وتعميمه بحيث يشمل الأمم السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the addressees’ creation through Adam and their intervening parents also implicitly recognizes all those ancestral links, as does mentioning God’s lordship over them.
rows.anchor: لأن خلقه تعالى للمأورين من نفس آدم عليه السلام حيث كانوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase وخلق منها زوجها coordinates with خلقكم inside the relative clause; repeating the verb distinguishes derivation from the original from creating a mate out of material.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على ( خلقكم ) داخل معه في حيز الصلة وأعيد الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mate is Eve, created from Adam’s left rib, as reported from Ibn Umar and others.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد من الزوج حواء وهي قد خلقت من ضلع آدم عليه السلام الأيسر كما روى ذلك عن ابن عمر وغيره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The two Sahih collections transmit the Prophet’s counsel to treat women well because they were created from a rib; its upper part is most crooked, and trying to straighten it breaks it while leaving it preserves its crookedness.
rows.anchor: وروى الشيخان استوصوا بالنساء خيرا فإنهن خلقن من ضلع وإن أعوج شيء من الضلع أعلاه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim denies that Eve was created from Adam’s rib, arguing that God could create her from dust and interpreting منها as “of the same kind,” like the phrase in 16:72.
rows.anchor: وأنكر أبو مسلم خلقها من الضلع لأنه سبحانه قادر على خلقها من التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some agree with Abu Muslim, saying the rib interpretation would mean Adam had intercourse with part of himself, which they find repugnant.
rows.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك بعضهم مدعيا أن القول بما ذكر يجر إلى القول بأن آدم عليه السلام كان ينكح بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Eve was a heavenly maiden created from the same substance as houris after Adam entered the Garden.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض أن حواء كانت حورية خلقت مما خلق منه الحور بعد أن أسكن آدم الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the houri view because no Quranic verse or hadith even hints at it; if houris were made from Paradise saffron, Eve would differ in kind from Adam, and if from Adam’s substance, the claim collapses into Abu Muslim’s position.
rows.anchor: أما الثاني فلأنه ليس في الآيات ولا الأحاديث ما يتوهم منه الإشارة إليه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu Muslim’s view because then humanity would come from two souls instead of the single soul stated here, and it conflicts with authentic Prophetic reports; this also undermines the houri view.
rows.anchor: وأما الأول فلأنه لو كان الأمر كما ذكر فيه لكان الناس مخلوقين من نفسين لا من نفس واحدة
